newsitem.title: USA: Excess rain a concern for Minnesota soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Excess rain a concern for Minnesota soybeans.

text.p: Rain in July produced excess moisture in Minnesota and during the week ended Sunday there was concern it would lead to diseases in soybeans, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service's weekly report.
"There is concern over the disease potential in soybeans if there is not drier weather soon," the report said.
Disease potential also exists for dry beans, sugarbeets, potatoes and small grains, the report said.
As of Sunday, soybeans setting pods reached 16 percent and 80 percent had bloomed versus nine and 65 percent, respectively, a year ago and the 17 and 66 averages.
Soybeans were rated 10 percent excellent, 49 good, 31 fair, seven poor and three very poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated 36 percent surplus, 61 adequate, and three short.

Corn advanced to five percent in the milk stage and 72 tasseling versus none and 42 a year ago, respectively, and the four and 53 averages. Corn was rated 18 percent excellent, 54 good, 22 fair, four poor and two very poor.

Spring wheat was 34 percent versus 34 a year ago and the 44 average. A small amount had been harvested versus two percent a year ago and for the average. Spring wheat was rated three percent excellent, 45 good, 40 fair, eight poor and four very poor.
Winter wheat was four percent harvested versus 18 a year ago and the 12 average.
Oats were 79 percent ripe versus 59 a year ago and the 67 average. The crop was rated three percent excellent, 44 good, 34 fair, six poor and 13 very poor.
